advisory.title: Preventing Card Testing: Spot It Early, Stop It Fast
advisory.rights_note: Short attributed excerpts quoted for analysis; full text remains at the source URL.
advisory.excerpt:
Card testing is when fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Fraud tactics are evolving, and card testing attacks are increasingly targeting e-commerce and mobile checkout.
They run $0 or small-dollar attempts at real merchants to confirm a card is active and may retry to fill in missing details (like CVV or expiration date).
Automated testing is the most common.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time—often from the same IP address, device or small set of sessions.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time (for example, cycling CVV or expiration date values).
A wave of $0 authorizations or low-dollar transactions used to test cards with minimal cost and attention.

dataset.description: Synthetic card-payments scenario (~3% fraud) with velocity, decline, and card-present features, including a deliberately injected card-testing pattern.
dataset.limitations: Fully synthetic. The card-testing pattern was injected to demonstrate how the workflow surfaces a coverage gap; results do not measure real-world detection.

findings.summary: J.P. Morgan Payments advisory on card testing attacks detailing how fraudsters use $0 or low-dollar transactions, automated cycling of card details (CVV/expiration), and high-frequency attempts from shared IPs or devices to test stolen cards.
behaviors: Fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Automated testing with many different card numbers attempted in a short time.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time.
indicators: Same IP address, device, or small set of sessions attempting many different card numbers.
Repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors resulting in more failed payments than usual.
Wave of $0 authorizations or low-dollar transactions.
testable_hypotheses: Transactions with small amounts and high 1-hour card frequency indicate card testing.
High declined attempts combined with high transaction frequency capture automated card testing waves.
uncertainties: Public security advisory does not provide quantitative thresholds or transaction logs.
Synthetic dataset lacks direct representation of IP addresses and device identifiers.

agent_conclusion.rationale: The intelligence document describes card testing attacks involving $0 or low-dollar transactions, rapid retry attempts, and multiple failed payments. While specific fields like IP address and device ID are unavailable in the evaluation dataset, the existing rule set (specifically RP-BASELINE-001 and AGT-a5193d19-3) already covers high-frequency declined card testing patterns. Evaluating a candidate rule for low-amount transactions combined with high 1-hour transaction frequency showed only marginal incremental recall while increasing false positives. Therefore, the advisory is already effectively covered by existing rules.
limitations: Synthetic dataset lacks device ID and IP address fields mentioned in the advisory.
Low amount candidate rule provides minimal incremental recall over the existing card-testing rule set.

rule.name: Low amount card testing velocity
rule.rationale: Tests small-dollar or $0 authorization card testing waves occurring in rapid succession within 1 hour.

baseline_rule.name: High transaction amount baseline
baseline_rule.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
baseline_rule.rationale: A simple, documented starting point for comparing candidate rules. The threshold is illustrative and is not calibrated for real financial data.

reference_rules.name: High transaction amount baseline
reference_rules.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
reference_rules.rationale: A simple, documented starting point for comparing candidate rules. The threshold is illustrative and is not calibrated for real financial data.

reference_rules.name: Card testing frequency and declines
reference_rules.rationale: Identifies cards undergoing multiple recent transactions combined with prior declined attempts.
